subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & model recommendations

Hi Alex / Sam —

Great chat today — thanks for walking us through the ACME summarization use case and the long legal docs workload. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Summary of what we heard
- Goal: end-to-end long-doc summarization for contracts and regulatory filings (16k–200k token documents).
- Key constraints: retain precision on clauses, maintain citation fidelity, avoid hallucinations, deterministic truncation behavior for streaming outputs.
- Current benchmark: internal ACME evaluation shows frequent entity truncation past ~12k tokens and some summary omission on nested sections.

2) Recommended models & initial eval plan
- Shortlist: RedWood-Optimized-16k (float16, KV-cache tuned), Llama2-70B-16k (float16), and a quantized 70B-32k candidate for evaluation. We recommend starting with RedWood-Optimized-16k for latency/cost balance and the quantized 32k candidate for any very long single-doc runs.
- Evaluation scope: precision/recall on clause extraction, citation alignment checks, truncation behavior tests, and summarization fidelity (human eval + automated ROUGE/QA checks).

3) Artifacts shared
- Prompt sets: attached file long_context_eval_prompt_set.csv (short/medium/long templates and edge-case prompts).
- Benchmarks: uploaded a preliminary comparison PDF (redwood-benchmarks-16k-compare.pdf) and the full run artifacts to the Drive link below.

4) Quality/regression concerns to watch for
- Truncation policy differences between model variants (some will drop prefixes, others favor most recent context) — we should test on the same prefix/window strategy.
- Summarization fidelity: aggressive extractive cues cause omission of nuanced clauses — will include targeted manual evals.
- Tokenization differences: align on tokenizer and byte offsets for citation mapping.

5) Next steps / mutual action plan
- ACME: share 10 representative documents and the internal rubric by Fri 2027-06-25. (requesting shared Drive folder + service account access)
- Redwood: spin up a 2-week eval sandbox with the three candidates, produce a side-by-side report, and schedule a review call week of 6/29.
- Pricing/PO: If results look good, we can prepare a Dedicated trial quote and suggested commit levels.

Would you prefer the review call on Tue 6/29 at 10am PT or Wed 6/30 at 11am PT?

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect, and I appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Documents: we'll share 12 files (mix of 20k–120k tokens). We'll create the folder and add a short rubric per document — target is to preserve clause-level citations and non-negotiable language when present.
2) Sandbox access: for the sandbox, do you need us to provide a VPC endpoint or will Redwood host within your dedicated eval env?
3) On the model shortlist — curious about the "RedWood-Optimized-16k" behavior on clause-long docs vs the quantized 32k. Can you share any latency ballpark for single-doc summarization (90th pctile) and token-cost guidance?

We can do Tue 6/29 10am PT.

Alex / Marissa / Sam —

Quick answers to the tech questions: 

- Sandbox hosting: we can offer a hosted eval sandbox (Redwood-hosted) with a temporary project token and an option to push into ACME VPC later. For initial runs we recommend Redwood-hosted to speed setup; we'll mirror the customer tokenization and runtime settings.
- Latency/cost: for RedWood-Optimized-16k on a 32GB GPU instance, single-doc summarization for a 40k-token document (split into overlapping windows with KV cache) typically finishes in ~22–35s p95 and costs are ~0.10–0.20 USD per 1k output tokens depending on truncation strategy. Quantized 32k runs on a 80GB instance: p95 ~45–70s, unit cost slightly lower per token but higher fixed infra cost. We'll provide a short benchmark matrix in the sandbox report.
- Truncation behavior: by default our runtime uses a sliding-window + KV-cache policy. We can run a secondary policy that preserves prefixes (useful for citations) if you want determinism for legal citations.

Attaching a quick checklist of runtime flags we'll use in the first pass (will include in the sandbox config).

—Dev
